title: Orthogonal finite subspaces pass from a dense subspace over a complete field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space with a definite norm $N:V\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ satisfying $N(-v)=N(v)$, $N(v+w)\le\max(N(v),N(w))$ and $N(av)=|a|N(v)$. Let $W\subseteq V$ be a $K$-linear subspace dense for $d(v,w)=N(v-w)$: every ball of positive radius in $V$ meets $W$. Suppose every finite-dimensional $K$-linear subspace $U\subseteq W$ has a finite basis $u_1,\ldots,u_n$ such that $$N\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i u_i\right)=\max_{1\le i\le n}|a_i|N(u_i)\qquad(a_i\in K).$$ Then every finite-dimensional $K$-linear subspace of $V$ has a basis with the same orthogonality property. The zero subspace has the empty basis, with maximum $0$. No completeness of $V$ or $W$, finite dimension of $V$, spherical completeness, or discreteness of the absolute value is assumed.
